title: State ponds in Lapland and Koillismaa listed for fishing leases
seoTitle: State ponds listed for fishing leases in Lapland
description: Metsähallitus has published its first public list of state waters open for fishing leases, including ponds in Posio, Rovaniemi, Salla and Kemijärvi.
dek: The list went online in early November with about a hundred ponds and lakes, each with its size, location and annual price, which starts at 90 euros plus VAT.
heroAlt: A small lake behind bare birches beside the road between Ruka and Posio: the first snow covers the ground and spruce forest lines the far shore.
heroCaption: By the Ruka–Posio road in October 2026. The waters on the lease list are small ponds away from villages and busy fishing spots.

body.text: Metsähallitus has published a list of the state waters whose fishing rights can be leased. It covers about a hundred ponds and lakes, and according to Metsähallitus a nationwide list of the waters on offer is being published for the first time.

body.title: Waters for lease in brief
items: List published: early November in the Eräluvat.fi service
Waters for lease in the Lapland region: 7
Annual rent: from 90 euros plus VAT
Length of lease: fixed term, no more than 10 years

body.text: What is on the list in the north

The Lapland region has seven waters on the list: Kuuliolampi in Kemijärvi, Lemmonlampi, Närhilampi and Pulkkalampi in Posio, Ristilampi and Salmilampi in Rovaniemi, and Pilkkasiipilampi in Salla. The smallest of them, Salmilampi, is 1.5 hectares and costs 90 euros a year plus VAT. The largest, Ristilampi, is 20.1 hectares and costs 218 euros.

In Koillismaa and along the Iijoki river the list is longer, and Kuusamo, Taivalkoski and Pudasjärvi each have several ponds on it. They include Riihilampi in Kuusamo at 9.1 hectares and 175 euros a year, Ahvenlampi in Taivalkoski at 12.9 hectares and 230 euros, and Mustosenlampi in Pudasjärvi at 14.9 hectares and 260 euros.
A lease does not close the water

A lease does not remove the general fishing rights that apply on the water. Anyone may still fish with a simple rod and line or ice fish free of charge, and lure fishing with one rod is allowed after paying the national fisheries management fee.

A lessee can apply to the Elinvoimakeskus authority to have those rights restricted, and the list shows for each pond whether that is possible at all. Metsähallitus says there are usually permit areas of its own near the leased waters.

items: Leases are fixed term, for no more than ten years, and the rent follows the cost-of-living index.
The lease covers fishing only. It gives no right of access and no right to off-road traffic, which needs a separate permit.
The lessee may build a boat rack, a fireplace of natural stones and a box for nets and gear. Anything else has to be agreed separately.
Stocking is allowed only for the fish species approved in the management plan of the fisheries area. Whitefish is the most common reason for leasing a pond.
Closing the water with fish barriers is not allowed.

body.text: Lessees can be private people or other non-profit organisations, and arrangements linked to business are agreed case by case. A fishing tourism company that wants a pond for its customers also needs a separate cooperation agreement. No lease agreements are made in wilderness areas, in protected areas or in the Sámi homeland.

There are 817 fishing leases in force at the moment, and together they cover less than two per cent of the state water areas managed by Metsähallitus. Olli Urpanen, who heads fishing at Metsähallitus, says the point of the list is openness: a person interested in a pond no longer has to contact the agency to find out what might be available.

A lease is requested on a form on the Eräluvat.fi site, and the waters are leased in the order the requests arrive. After that the request goes to a fisheries specialist at Metsähallitus, and the contract sets out detailed conditions for using the water.
Why cold, clean water is one of the most valuable things in northern nature is explained on our freshwater page.
